methods.name: _overview
methods.summary: Whether Docker can be reached, and every container and Compose stack it has. A Docker that cannot be reached is an answer (`engine.reachable` is false and says why), not an error.

methods.name: _connect
methods.summary: Choose the Docker this app manages, and answer with what it has.

params.name: host
params.description: Where Docker listens: `unix:///path/docker.sock`, `tcp://host:2375` or `http://host:2375`. Empty for this machine's own Docker.

errors.message: The address is not one Docker can be reached at.

methods.name: _start
methods.summary: Start a container.

params.name: container
params.description: The id of one of the containers of `overview`.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, the container or stack is gone, or Docker refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _stop
methods.summary: Stop a container: Docker asks it to end, and kills it after ten seconds.

params.name: container
params.description: The id of one of the containers of `overview`.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, the container or stack is gone, or Docker refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _restart
methods.summary: Stop a container and start it again.

params.name: container
params.description: The id of one of the containers of `overview`.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, the container or stack is gone, or Docker refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _remove
methods.summary: Remove a container. A running one only when `force`, which kills it first. Its named volumes stay; its anonymous volumes too, unless `volumes`.

params.name: container
params.description: The id of one of the containers of `overview`.

params.name: force
params.description: Remove it even while it runs: Docker kills it first.

params.name: volumes
params.description: Also remove the anonymous volumes it was made with.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, the container or stack is gone, or Docker refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _create
methods.summary: Make a container from a spec: the image is pulled first when Docker does not have it (`_pulling` tells how that goes), and the container is started when `start`. A container that could not be made and started is not left behind.

errors.message: What was asked for is not a container Docker can make (the message says what is wrong), or Docker cannot be reached or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _recreate
methods.summary: Make a container again from a changed spec, as Docker cannot change one: the old one is stopped and removed, the new one made with its name and started when the old one ran (or `start`). When that fails the old one is made again from its own settings, and started when it ran. Anything it kept outside a volume is lost.

params.name: container
params.description: The id of one of the containers of `overview`.

errors.message: What was asked for is not a container Docker can make (the message says what is wrong), or Docker cannot be reached or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _networks
methods.summary: Docker's networks, by name, each with the containers on it: what a container can be put on.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _volumes
methods.summary: Docker's volumes, by name, each with the containers that use it: what a container can mount.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _volume_create
methods.summary: Make a volume, and answer with the volumes there are now. A name another volume has is refused.

params.name: name
params.description: Its name; empty for one Docker makes up.

params.name: driver
params.description: The driver that keeps it; empty for `local`.

errors.message: What was asked for is not a volume Docker can make (the message says what is wrong), or Docker cannot be reached or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _volume_remove
methods.summary: Remove a volume, and the data in it. One a container uses, running or not, is refused, naming the containers.

params.name: volume
params.description: The name of one of the volumes of `_volumes`.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _volumes_prune
methods.summary: Remove every volume no container uses, named or not, and the data in them.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _network_create
methods.summary: Make a network, and answer with the networks there are now.

params.name: driver
params.description: `bridge`, `overlay`, `macvlan`, `ipvlan`, or a plugin's; empty for `bridge`.

params.name: subnet
params.description: The addresses it gives out (`172.30.0.0/16`); empty for Docker to choose.

params.name: gateway
params.description: Its gateway, an address in `subnet`; empty for Docker to choose.

params.name: internal
params.description: Its containers reach each other, not the world.

params.name: attachable
params.description: A container can join it by hand (a swarm network).

errors.message: What was asked for is not a network Docker can make (the message says what is wrong), or Docker cannot be reached or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _network_remove
methods.summary: Remove a network. Docker's own cannot be removed, nor one a running container is on.

params.name: network
params.description: The name of one of the networks of `_networks`.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _images
methods.summary: The images Docker has, each with the containers made from it.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _image_pull
methods.summary: Pull an image from its registry, newer or not (`_pulling` tells how that goes), and answer with the images there are now.

params.name: image
params.description: Its name: `nginx`, `nginx:1.27`, `ghcr.io/owner/app:1.0`.

errors.message: That is not the name of an image, the registry does not have it, or Docker cannot be reached or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _image_remove
methods.summary: Remove an image, with all its names. One a container was made from only when `force`, and never one a running container was made from.

params.name: image
params.description: The id of one of the images of `_images`.

params.name: force
params.description: Remove it though a stopped container was made from it.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _images_prune
methods.summary: Remove the dangling images: those with no name that no container was made from.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, or refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _recipes
methods.summary: The image recipes, by the name of their image: each the Dockerfile an image of that name is built from, and what its last build left.

methods.name: _add_recipe
methods.summary: Keep a new recipe, and answer with the recipes there are now. Nothing is built until `_build`.

params.name: tag
params.description: The name the image is built as, with its tag: `tools:1`, `ghcr.io/owner/tools:1`. A name without a tag is `:latest`.

params.name: dockerfile
params.description: The Dockerfile: the whole build context. What the image needs, it downloads.

errors.message: The name is not one of an image, another recipe builds it, or the Dockerfile is empty: the message says which.

methods.name: _update_recipe
methods.summary: Change a recipe's name or Dockerfile, and answer with the recipes there are now. What its last build left stays; the next build builds the recipe as it is then.

params.name: recipe
params.description: The id of one of the recipes of `_recipes`.

params.name: tag
params.description: The name the image is built as, with its tag: `tools:1`, `ghcr.io/owner/tools:1`. A name without a tag is `:latest`.

params.name: dockerfile
params.description: The Dockerfile: the whole build context. What the image needs, it downloads.

errors.message: The name is not one of an image, another recipe builds it, or the Dockerfile is empty: the message says which.

methods.name: _remove_recipe
methods.summary: Remove a recipe, and answer with the recipes there are now. The images it built stay: they are removed with `_image_remove`.

params.name: recipe
params.description: The id of one of the recipes of `_recipes`.

errors.message: There is no such recipe.

methods.name: _build
methods.summary: Start a build of a recipe's image from its Dockerfile, and answer at once with the recipes (it is `building`). `_building` tells how it goes. The name moves to the new image, as `docker build -t` does. A build of it that is under way goes on, and no second one starts.

params.name: recipe
params.description: The id of one of the recipes of `_recipes`.

errors.message: There is no such recipe.

methods.name: _stack_start
methods.summary: Start every container of a Compose stack, the services others depend on first.

params.name: stack
params.description: The name of one of the stacks of `overview`.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, the container or stack is gone, or Docker refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _stack_stop
methods.summary: Stop every container of a Compose stack, the services others depend on last.

params.name: stack
params.description: The name of one of the stacks of `overview`.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, the container or stack is gone, or Docker refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _stack_restart
methods.summary: Stop a Compose stack and start it again.

params.name: stack
params.description: The name of one of the stacks of `overview`.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, the container or stack is gone, or Docker refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _stack_remove
methods.summary: Take a Compose stack down: remove its containers and its networks. Its volumes stay.

params.name: stack
params.description: The name of one of the stacks of `overview`.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, the container or stack is gone, or Docker refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _details
methods.summary: What a container was made with: what it runs, its health, what is mounted, its networks, and its spec (the settings a new container is made with, as the form has them). Its environment's values are sent: the window hides them until they are asked for.

params.name: container
params.description: The id of one of the containers of `overview`.

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, the container or stack is gone, or Docker refused: the message says which.

methods.name: _logs
methods.summary: The end of what a container has written, both its output and its errors, as text.

params.name: container
params.description: The id of one of the containers of `overview`.

params.name: tail
params.description: How many lines from the end (200 when left out).

errors.message: Docker cannot be reached, the container or stack is gone, or Docker refused: the message says which.

methods.name: list_containers
methods.summary: List the containers
methods.description: Every Docker container of this machine, running or not: its name, image, state (running, exited, paused, ...), Docker's own words for it (`Up 2 hours`), its published ports (`8080:80`) and the Compose stack it belongs to (empty for a container on its own). Give `stack` for the containers of one stack only.

params.name: stack
params.description: The name of a Compose stack; every container when left out

methods.name: container_logs
methods.summary: Read a container's logs
methods.description: The end of what a container has written (its output and its errors together), by the container's name (`list_containers` gives the names).

params.name: container
params.description: The name of the container

params.name: lines
params.description: How many lines from the end; 200 when left out

methods.name: list_images
methods.summary: List the images
methods.description: Every image Docker has: its id, its names (`nginx:1.27`; none for a dangling one), its size in bytes, when it was built (seconds since 1970) and the names of the containers made from it.

methods.name: list_volumes
methods.summary: List the volumes
methods.description: Every volume Docker has: its name, driver, where its data is, when it was made and the names of the containers that mount it.

methods.name: list_networks
methods.summary: List the networks
methods.description: Every network Docker has: its name, driver, scope, subnet and gateway, whether it is internal or attachable, whether it is one of Docker's own, and the names of the containers on it.

methods.name: start_container
methods.summary: Start a container
methods.description: Start a stopped container, by its name.

params.name: container
params.description: The name of the container

methods.name: stop_container
methods.summary: Stop a container
methods.description: Stop a running container, by its name: Docker asks it to end and kills it after ten seconds.

params.name: container
params.description: The name of the container

methods.name: restart_container
methods.summary: Restart a container
methods.description: Stop a container and start it again, by its name.

params.name: container
params.description: The name of the container

methods.name: start_stack
methods.summary: Start a stack
methods.description: Start every container of a Compose stack, by the stack's name (`list_containers` gives each container's stack). The services others wait for start first.

params.name: stack
params.description: The name of the stack

methods.name: stop_stack
methods.summary: Stop a stack
methods.description: Stop every container of a Compose stack, by the stack's name. Nothing is removed.

params.name: stack
params.description: The name of the stack

methods.name: _pulling
methods.summary: How the pull of an image goes, while `_create` or `_recreate` waits for it.

params.name: status
params.description: Docker's word for the step it is at: `Downloading`, `Extracting`, ...

params.name: current
params.description: How many bytes of the image's layers are downloaded.

params.name: total
params.description: How many bytes there are to download, as far as Docker has said; 0 while it has not.

methods.name: _building
methods.summary: How the build of a recipe's image goes, a line at a time: Docker's output while it runs, then a last line that says it is done or why it failed. Read the recipes and the images again once it is over.

params.name: recipe
params.description: The id of the recipe whose image is built.

params.name: line
params.description: A line of the build's output, or the last line: the image it made, or why it failed.

params.name: status
params.description: `running` while the build goes on, `done` when it made the image, `failed` when it did not.

methods.name: changed
methods.summary: Docker changed (a container, an image, a volume or a network), or a tool changed something: the open windows read again what they show.

version.description: Docker's version, empty when it cannot be reached.

host.description: Where Docker is looked for, as given to `connect`. Empty for this machine's own Docker.

problem.description: Why Docker cannot be reached, as a sentence. Empty when it can.

status.description: Docker's own words for the state: `Up 2 hours`, `Exited (0) 3 days ago`.

ports.description: The published ports, each as `8080:80` (the machine's port, then the container's).

stack.description: The Compose stack it belongs to; empty for a container on its own.

service.description: Its service in the stack; empty for a container on its own.

running.description: How many of its containers are running.

folder.description: The folder it was brought up from; empty when Compose did not record one.

containers.description: Every container, running or not, by name.

stacks.description: The Compose stacks the containers belong to, by name.

command.description: What it runs, as one line.

health.description: `healthy`, `unhealthy` or `starting` for a container with a health check; empty without one.

mounts.description: Each mount as `source -> path in the container`, `(read-only)` after one it cannot write; the image's own volumes too.

truncated.description: The text is the end of something longer.

Listed.description: A container as an agent reads it in a list.

Entry.description: A name and its value: a variable of the environment, or a label.

Port.description: A port of the container, published on the machine.

host_ip.description: The machine's address it is published on; empty for all of them.

host_port.description: The machine's port, 1 to 65535; empty for one Docker chooses.

MountKind.description: `bind`: a folder of the machine. `volume`: a volume of Docker's.

Mount.description: What a container finds at a place of its own.

source.description: A bind mount's folder, a whole path; a volume's name (made when there is none), empty for an anonymous one.

target.description: Where in the container, a whole path.

Restart.description: When Docker starts the container again: never, always, unless it was stopped by hand, or after it failed.

Spec.description: The settings a container is made with, as the form has them. What is empty is the image's own, or Docker's.

name.description: Its name; empty for one Docker chooses.

command.description: What the entrypoint is given in place of the image's command, as words a shell would split.

entrypoint.description: What it runs in place of the image's entrypoint, as words a shell would split.

publish_all.description: Also publish every port the image exposes, each on a port Docker chooses.

network.description: The network it is put on: `bridge` for Docker's own.

retries.description: With `on-failure`: how many times at most, a whole number; empty or 0 for no limit.

working_dir.description: The folder it starts in, a whole path; empty for the image's.

user.description: Who it runs as (`1000`, `1000:1000`, `nginx`); empty for the image's.

hostname.description: Its host name; empty for Docker's.

start.description: Start it once it is made.

Made.description: A container that was made, and what Docker has now.

Network.description: A network of Docker's, and the containers on it.

scope.description: `local`: this machine only; `swarm`: every node of a swarm.

subnet.description: The addresses it gives out, as its IPAM has them (`172.18.0.0/16`); several are joined by `, `. Empty when Docker chose none.

gateway.description: Its gateway, as its IPAM has it; several are joined by `, `. Empty when Docker chose none.

internal.description: Its containers reach each other, not the world.

attachable.description: A container can join it by hand (a swarm network).

predefined.description: One of Docker's own (`bridge`, `host`, `none`): every Docker has them, and none can be removed.

containers.description: The names of the containers put on it, running or not.

Volume.description: A volume of Docker's, and the containers that use it.

mountpoint.description: Where its data is on the machine Docker runs on.

created.description: When it was made, as Docker says (RFC 3339); empty when Docker does not say.

containers.description: The names of the containers that mount it, running or not.

Image.description: An image Docker has, and the containers made from it.

tags.description: Its names (`nginx:1.27`); none for a dangling image, which a newer image of its name took the name of.

size.description: How much of the disk it takes, in bytes.

created.description: When it was built, in seconds since 1970.

containers.description: The names of the containers made from it, running or not.

ImagesPruned.description: What a prune of the dangling images removed, and the images there are now.

space.description: How much of the disk was freed, in bytes.

BuildStatus.description: How a build of an image goes: under way, done, or failed.

Recipe.description: An image recipe: the name an image is built as, and the Dockerfile it is built from.

tag.description: The name the image is built as, with its tag: `tools:1`.

dockerfile.description: The Dockerfile, the whole build context.

image.description: The id of the image the last build that worked made; empty when none has.

current.description: That image was built from the recipe as it is now: neither its name nor its Dockerfile changed since.

problem.description: Why the last build failed; empty when it worked, or there was none.

building.description: A build of it is under way.

VolumesPruned.description: What a prune of the unused volumes removed, and the volumes there are now.

removed.description: The names of the volumes that went, with their data.

space.description: How much of the disk was freed, in bytes.
